title: Power of Four
description: Given a 32-bit signed integer `n`, return `true` if it is a power of four (that is, there exists an integer `x >= 0` such that `n == 4^x`), and `false` otherwise. Solve it in O(1) time without loops or recursion.
hints: First verify `n > 0` and `(n & (n - 1)) == 0` so that `n` is a positive power of two.
A power of two is a power of four if and only if its single set bit sits at an even bit index (0, 2, 4, ...), which can be tested with `0x55555555`.

examples.explanation: 5 is not a power of four, so return false.
